niche: Mind Hacks, AI Secrets, Bizarre Body Science & Hidden Power Dynamics

ideas.title: Why Websites Check Your Exact Battery Percentage
ideas.angle: Demonstrates the hidden Battery Status API used by tracking brokers to uniquely profile and track your device across incognito tabs without cookies. Drives massive comments by challenging viewers to drop their exact current battery percentage in the chat to see who shares their digital profile.

hook.en: Check your battery percentage right now.

ideas.reason: Battery status fingerprinting is a trending cyber-privacy exploit exposed in computer science journals, offering an immediate tangible hook that every smartphone viewer can instantly verify.
sources: Princeton Web Transparency & Accountability Project (Battery Status API Leaks)
W3C Battery Status API Privacy Analysis

ideas.title: The Secret Invisible Watermark Inside AI Images
ideas.angle: Exposes SynthID and zero-bit steganography embedded into AI-generated images and audio, showing viewers how platforms instantly flag synthetic media even after cropping. Sparks viewer engagement by asking them if platforms should legally be forced to mark AI faces in their feeds.

hook.en: Look closely at this AI image.

ideas.reason: With deepfake legislation and Google SynthID integration dominating tech headlines, revealing the imperceptible math hidden in synthetic pixels creates high-retention curiosity.
sources: IEEE Transactions on Information Forensics and Security

ideas.title: Your Home Wi-Fi Can See Through Walls
ideas.angle: Reveals Wi-Fi Channel State Information (CSI) sensing, showing how everyday routers map human silhouettes and breathing movements through walls without cameras. Concludes with an urgent privacy takeaway on turning off smart home sniffing, triggering viral shares and comment debates.

hook.en: Your Wi-Fi router is watching you.

ideas.reason: Wi-Fi sensing (IEEE 802.11bf) has recently become a mainstream consumer tech standard, triggering shock factor and hyper-defensive curiosity among smart-home owners.
sources: Carnegie Mellon University Wi-Fi DensePose Research
